items.hed: The Veil Is a Filter, Not a Wall
items.body: Gnostic teachers spoke of the veil between the apparent world and the real as something that thins with attention — not a brick barrier. Tuesday’s residual weather is noise on the screen; the charge underneath is still yours. Practice seeing the filter for what it is: weather, inbox, feed — then choose what passes through.

Classical Hermetica pairs the elements: water dissolves form; fire concentrates will. A wet forecast is not a soft day unless you let it be. Keep the inner fire (breath, plank, next clear move) while the outer water does its work. Coherence under weather is the real alchemy.

In esoteric practice, to name a force is to place it. Name the morning: charge, body, security skim, then the rest. Unnamed urgency owns you; named urgency becomes a task with a place on the page. Forbidden knowledge, stripped of theater, is often just precise naming.

openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Tomorrow’s gate is the same: breath under residual weather — not the forecast, not the feed. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Then own the day.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Dom does not wait for clear skies to start. Fierce calm is competitive composure when the radar is loud: charge first, body second, security skim when ready, admin only after the morning has already won. One breath, one move, one clear next step. Competitors may arrive loud; he arrives prepared. When pressure rises, he slows the breath, names the next action, and outlasts the noise. Tomorrow is not about proving anything. It is about starting clean so the rest of the week has room to land.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Run this after Morning Charge — box breathing first, then the body. Residual weather outside; heat inside. Then news and the day.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time. Optional: Front Clips / Back Clips if you want a second RipStick move.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.hed: Establish Your Steps Before You Run
grimoire.body: “The heart of man plans his way, but the Lord establishes his steps.” (Proverbs 16:9) Solomon’s counsel is not against planning — it is against rushing an unestablished plan. A morning that opens with charge and body establishes the steps; the inbox and the radar become secondary weather. Classical lore cast Solomon as one who ordered the court before the petition. Order the morning the same way — breath first, body second, then the board.
grimoire.practice: Finish Opening Bell and the 3-minute opener before any security skim. Establish the step; then walk it.

techDemo.kicker: Fast learn · from your X bookmarks
techDemo.pick: SpaceXAI engineer Lauren Tan — GrokBot as a team (Chief of Staff → Managers → Workers), not one chat window
techDemo.author: @Dmytroo_eth

image.alt: GrokBot org chart — Chief of Staff to Managers to Workers to autonomous workflow

lesson.oneLiner: Stop living in one chat. Promote the work: Chief of Staff routes → Managers own lanes → Workers execute → Skills + workflows run overnight.
beats: Chief of Staff = the router that prioritizes and assigns (not the doer of every task).
Managers = 3 lane owners who keep context and hand off clean jobs.
Workers = specialists that actually ship research / build / launch pieces.
Skills + autonomous workflows = the glue so accepted work keeps moving without you babysitting.
Tan’s punchline: 20+ agents organized beats one mega-thread wondering why everything is slow.
lesson.takeaway: Under a minute: if you’re still one window deep, spend one evening standing up CoS → Managers → Workers — then Research → Build → Launch → Improve.
